title: mledoze/countries
note: Widely-used, MIT-licensed country metadata dataset (backs many published npm country-data packages). Downloaded the full countries.json directly and extracted Uganda's entry (cca2=UG) with a script, not a summarizer, to avoid truncation (the file is ~1.4MB; an initial WebFetch attempt got cut off before reaching entries starting with 'U'). Source for name/ISO codes/currency/calling code/capital/region/languages/tld/borders/area/demonyms/flag emoji in data/country/uganda.json.

title: File:Flag_of_Uganda.svg
note: Downloaded via the Special:FilePath redirect and visually verified (black/yellow/red bands, grey crowned crane) before use. Public domain per Commons' file page: ineligible for copyright (simple geometric/national symbol) and expired under Uganda's Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act 2004's non-retrospective provision. Carries a standard 'insignia' usage caveat: national symbol use is independently restricted in many countries regardless of copyright status. Stored at data/country/assets/flag.svg and flag.png (960x640 raster render).

title: File:Coat_of_arms_of_Uganda.svg
note: Downloaded via the Special:FilePath redirect and visually verified (kob antelope + crested crane supporters, sun, drum, spears, 'FOR GOD AND MY COUNTRY' motto banner) before use. Licensed CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported — attribution and share-alike required, which is STRICTER than this project's default CC-BY 4.0 data license (see LICENSE-DATA.md). Stored at data/country/assets/coat-of-arms.svg and coat-of-arms.png (960x1029 raster render).

title: Web search: Uganda time zone and driving side
publisher: Aggregated from timeanddate.com, Wikipedia (Time in Uganda), and driving-in-Uganda travel guides
note: Confirmed Uganda observes East Africa Time (EAT, UTC+03:00) year-round with no DST, and drives on the left (former British colony convention). Both are extremely stable, long-established facts, cross-checked across multiple independent results rather than a single source.

title: Statoids: Districts in Uganda
note: Page states last updated April 2026. Used to cross-check the 135-district count and region groupings.

title: Districts of Uganda
note: Cross-checked district list and region totals (135 as of 2020 baseline, still current at district-count level).

title: List of Local Governments in Uganda

title: Counties of Uganda
note: Wikitext table mechanically parsed (see data/legacy/provenance/parse_counties.mjs). Reflects county/district structure as of ~2015 (167 counties, 23 municipal councils) predating the 2016-2020 wave of new districts. Superseded entirely by src-ec-admin-units-2022's county layer (2022, verified, covers all 136 rural districts) — no longer ingested into the build; kept at data/legacy/counties_2015_statoids.csv for provenance only. One item flagged in an earlier pass as a likely source error — a 'Ik County' row under Kaabong District that looked like a duplicate/anomaly — was independently confirmed real by the 2022 EC data (Ik County is a genuine, small Kaabong constituency/county), so that flag was wrong and has been retracted; a 'Nakifuma Council' row that doesn't cleanly fit its rowspan group remains unexplained.

title: Uganda - Subnational Administrative Boundaries (COD-AB)
publisher: OCHA / Humanitarian Data Exchange, sourced from UBOS
note: USED FOR P-CODES ONLY (final state, 2026-10-17); not a source of unit names/lists and no longer a source of published geometry. Originally (2026-07-09) evaluated as a bulk name source and rejected below district level as stale — that verdict stands: it is the 2020 system (valid_on 2020-08-24, licence CC BY-IGO), with exactly ADM0-ADM4 = country, 4 regions, 135 districts (no Terego), 203 counties, 1,520 subcounties, and NO parish or village level (the original note read its ~208 admin3 / ~1,520 admin4 features as too-thin subcounty/parish counts; they are in fact the county and subcounty tiers — see the retraction in src-hdx-cod-ab-uga-admin4-parish). HISTORY: earlier on 2026-10-17 an intermediate build used COD-AB's polygons as the district (ADM2), county (ADM3, 118 of 322) and subcounty (ADM4, 1,351 of 2,191) geometry, after a direct comparison showed they were far more accurate than geoBoundaries' district layer (only 12 of 135 geoBoundaries districts had IoU >= 0.9 with their COD-AB/UBOS counterpart; geoBoundaries' Kampala was 351 km2 vs ~189 official, having swallowed Kira and Kasangati, which are in Wakiso; Pader town fell inside Agago). That build was superseded the same day by UBOS's own current polygons (src-ubos-nphc-2024-geo, src-ubos-bec-2025-geo), which cover every level including parishes and need no 2020-to-2022 name matching; COD-AB's scripts/ingest-district-boundaries.mjs and scripts/ingest-subcounty-boundaries.mjs were deleted. WHAT IT IS USED FOR NOW: data/crosswalk/hdx-cod-ab-uga.csv, the P-code crosswalk written by scripts/ingest-hdx-cod-ab.mjs (matched within each district family on base name AND tier; adm1 4/4 exact; adm2 135 exact + 1 split_from (Terego -> UG3072); adm3 117 exact, 10 predecessor, 66 unmatched, 5 tier_mismatch, 4 no_equivalent, 1 rejected_geometry; adm4 1,352 exact, 146 unmatched, 21 tier_mismatch, 1 rejected_geometry), which populates external_refs.hdx_pcode (1,608 units) and external_refs.hdx_within_pcode (all 2,663 eligible units) and the hdx_pcode property on boundary features. COD-AB's polygons are read only to sanity-check each name match against the UBOS-derived districts (scripts/lib/fit-to-district.mjs with { clip: false } — a test, nothing is clipped or published) and, since 2026-10-17, as the second comparison in scripts/compare-boundaries.mjs (hdx_iou in data/qa/boundary-agreement.csv: median IoU 0.753 across 1,352 subcounties — low because COD-AB is the 2018-2020 system and many units have split since, so it is context, not a defect, and not used for the review flag); with UBOS districts as the reference it rejects just 2 matches, both on the Masindi-Kiryandongo line — county Bujenje (UG412501) and subcounty Pakanyi (UG41250103), which COD-AB places mostly inside Kiryandongo while UBOS and the EC have them in Masindi — so those two P-codes are withheld. One hand-confirmed rename is matched by P-code (PCODE_OVERRIDES: Central Division UG10080101 -> subcounty:kampala-kampala-central). Raw files are not committed (gitignored at data/legacy/provenance/geo/hdx-cod-ab/); re-fetch via the CKAN API URL above — HDX may return 403 to non-browser user agents, a curl request with a browser User-Agent works. The crosswalk and P-code fields carry CC BY-IGO attribution to OCHA/UBOS — see LICENSE-DATA.md.

title: Electoral Commission of Uganda
note: Identified as the deepest authoritative source. Initial WebFetch-tool requests to ec.or.ug pages returned HTTP 403; a direct request with a standard browser user-agent succeeded (see src-ec-admin-units-2022), which is where the actual village-level bulk data and its provenance are documented. Polling-station-level data (50,739 stations reported for 2025/26) is separate from the administrative-unit gazetteer and remains un-ingested.

title: FULL LIST: Govt approves nine new town councils ahead of 2026 elections
note: Reports 9 new town councils effective 2025-07-01. Direct fetch returned HTTP 403 during research, so the specific list of names/districts is UNVERIFIED and intentionally not included in data/ yet. Needs a primary-source re-check.

title: Uganda's Verified Administrative Units, July 2022 (full village-level gazetteer) + Summary of Administrative Units After Verification, June 2022
note: The genuine bulk source this project was missing: a 3,019-page PDF listing every district > constituency > subcounty/town/division > parish/ward > village in Uganda (146 district-equivalent units, 353 constituencies, 2,191 subcounties/towns/divisions, 10,717 parishes/wards, 71,230 villages), plus a companion 4-page summary-statistics PDF with the same totals per district. Direct WebFetch requests to ec.or.ug returned HTTP 403; the files downloaded fine via a direct request with a standard browser user-agent. Parsed with a custom coordinate-aware script (data/legacy/provenance/ec/parse_admin_units.mjs) because plain text extraction destroys the nested table structure. Validated twice: (1) every one of the ~2,198 'TOTAL VILLAGES IN <subcounty>' checksums printed in the source document itself matches the parser's accumulated count, and (2) fully re-aggregated per-district totals (villages, subcounties, parishes, constituencies) match the companion summary PDF exactly for all 146 districts/cities, zero discrepancies. This is what confirmed Terego District was missing from the original 135-district baseline (it is included here as district-equivalent #142 of 146). Promoted to confidence: verified in data/ec/. Caveat: dated July 2022 — does not reflect any 2023-2026 changes (e.g. the reported-but-unverified 2025/2026 new town councils, see src-monitor-town-councils-2025).

title: User-supplied research cross-checking EC constituency data as a current county source (Manafwa/Namisindwa, Nebbi/Pakwach, Nakapiripirit/Nabilatuk, Hoima/Kikuube, Kaabong/Karenga, Kibaale/Kagadi/Kakumiro)
publisher: UBOS National Population and Housing Census drilldown (statistics.ubos.org/nphc/drilldown), Wikipedia district pages, and several Google AI Mode conversation shares (share.google/aimode/...)
note: User-provided research used to test whether EC 'constituency' names (src-ec-admin-units-2022) are usable as current county names outside city/Kampala divisions. Checked against 13 districts: 11 matched exactly, and 2 (Nakapiripirit, Kikuube) showed the EC data has one additional split the cited sources didn't mention (Chekwii -> Chekwii + Chekwii East; Buhaguzi -> Buhaguzi + Buhaguzi East) — a refinement, not a contradiction. This result is what justified the county-promotion logic in scripts/ingest-ec-admin-units.mjs. Caveat: the share.google/aimode links are AI Mode conversation shares, not primary documents, and were not independently re-fetched/verified by the assistant — treated as corroborating signal alongside the UBOS/Wikipedia links, not as a primary source in their own right. The county layer's actual confidence rests on src-ec-admin-units-2022's own two independent validation passes, not on this cross-check alone.

title: UBOS National Population and Housing Census 2024 — dissemination API, geospatial data (district and subcounty polygons)
note: USED — with src-ubos-bec-2025-geo, the geometry source for EVERY published boundary layer (parish, subcounty, county, city, district, and the regions dissolved from districts) since 2026-10-17, replacing both geoBoundaries and an intermediate same-day OCHA COD-AB build. The district call returns 147 features: 136 districts plus the 10 cities as separate districts, with Kampala in 2 features; the per-district subcounty calls return 2,206 features under 2,205 codes; features carry 2024 population (male/female/total). UBOS codes nest by prefix: district 3 digits, county 4 (district + 1), subcounty 6 (county + 2) — and the BEC parish codes extend the same scheme (subcounty + 2). Snapshotted 2026-10-17 by the research/observatory session (scripts/observatory/fetch-public-sources.mjs on branch research/observatory — 303 files across this entry and src-ubos-bec-2025-geo, no failures, one request per second, URL/bytes/sha256 per file in manifest-observatory.json) and copied into this branch's data/legacy/provenance/ubos/ (gitignored; re-fetch from the URLs above). Consumed by scripts/ingest-ubos-boundaries.mjs, which never creates a unit from UBOS: names and the tree stay the EC's (src-ec-admin-units-2022), and UBOS land is attached to EC units under the territorial rule (docs/DATA_QUALITY.md). UBOS subcounties vs EC subcounty-tier units, by name and tier within the district: 2,105 exact, 7 fuzzy, 75 carved_from (UBOS subcounties created after the EC's July 2022 gazetteer — their land is assigned to the EC subcounty most of their parishes came from), 18 unmatched (15 of them refugee-settlement census units — see below; the other 3 are Iceme, Nyakabungo and Kiryandongo Town Councils, where the build's 3 inferred subcounties landed). Results recorded per unit in data/crosswalk/ubos-2024.csv and as external_refs.ubos_code. REFUGEE SETTLEMENTS (updated 2026-10-17): the 15 settlement census units were at first shipped as 11 subcounty-level gaps (~869 km2); they are now split between the touching host subcounties of the same district along equidistant (nearest-neighbour) lines — inferred, since no source records the real lines — and each settlement's outline is published as an informational layer, data/geo/settlements.geojson (id settlement:<ubos code>, name, ubos_code, district_id, host_subcounty_ids, note). POPULATION (added 2026-10-17): the per-subcounty 2024 population these features carry is now used — each UBOS subcounty's figure goes to the EC subcounty that owns its land (name match, or the unit it was carved from), settlement units excluded and '#N/A' values skipped (no figure rather than 0), written to data/population/ubos-nphc-2024-subcounty.csv: 2,180 subcounties, 44,986,031 people vs the 45,905,417 national total (the ~919k difference is the settlement units, counted separately); approximate where a UBOS subcounty's parishes were reorganised across EC units (method column: name_match | includes_carved_units). scripts/build.mjs attaches it to subcounty features and sums it to counties (partial: true where a subcounty has no figure). AGREEMENT CHECK (added 2026-10-17): scripts/compare-boundaries.mjs compares each published subcounty with this source's polygon for the same UBOS code (IoU over the unit's district land): median 0.991 across 2,110 subcounties; the 7 below 0.8 are all refugee-settlement hosts that absorbed settlement land — see data/qa/boundary-agreement.csv. LICENCE: UBOS's usage guidelines allow reproduction with citation to UBOS and a link to the source; processed data must be labelled as processed — every boundary layer here is processed UBOS data (see LICENSE-DATA.md). The county-level call (313 features) was fetched but is not used: counties are unions of their EC subcounties, so they always agree with the subcounty layer.

title: UBOS Baseline Education Census (BEC) 2025 — API, parish polygons
note: USED — the only official, current PARISH polygons found anywhere; the base of the whole bottom-up build in scripts/ingest-ubos-boundaries.mjs (every subcounty, county, city and district is a union of this parish land). 10,831 parish features with 8-digit codes (the UBOS subcounty code + 2 digits — every parish code's first 6 digits is its UBOS subcounty code) and school/learner counts for the requested indicator. Fetched in the same research/observatory snapshot as src-ubos-nphc-2024-geo (copied into data/legacy/provenance/ubos/, gitignored). Matched to EC (July 2022) parishes within each district by name, with tier words ('ward', 'town council', 'TC', 'TOWNCOUNCIL') normalised; a name repeated inside a district is disambiguated by its subcounty; a unique near-miss spelling (edit distance <= 1 for names of 6+ characters, <= 2 for 10+) is accepted only inside the expected subcounty. Result: 10,466 exact + 98 fuzzy matches, 267 UBOS parishes unmatched (their land still belongs to a subcounty, and where a subcounty has exactly one unmatched EC parish and land left over, that land is inferred to be the parish — 73 parishes). Published: 10,634 of the EC's 10,717 parishes/wards (99.2%) in data/geo/parishs.geojson, per-unit matches in data/crosswalk/ubos-2024.csv. Same licence terms as src-ubos-nphc-2024-geo: cite UBOS with a link; processed data labelled as processed. TOPOLOGY CLEANING (added 2026-10-17): these polygons were not drawn as one topology — per district they overlap their neighbours by ~0.3-0.4 km2 (65-99 overlapping pairs) and leave ~4 km2 of gaps against the district outline in 1,000-1,800 slivers (Alebtong: 4.25 km2 in ~1,854 parts). scripts/lib/tessellate.mjs cleans each district before anything is built: clip to the UBOS district polygon (land only), give overlaps to the parish earlier in UBOS-code order, ignore gaps < 100 m2, give gaps <= 2 ha whole to the nearest neighbour, split 2 ha-5 km2 between the touching parishes by nearest-neighbour allocation, and publish anything > 5 km2 as a gap. National totals: 53.2 km2 of overlaps removed, 409.5 km2 of gaps filled (43,157 slivers, 5,307 equidistant splits), 1 piece fully overlapped (Lubya, Buvuma, 12010603 — which therefore has no polygon), 0 unassigned chunks. Alebtong's gaps went from 4.25 to 0.067 km2. Since the refugee-settlement units' parishes are now split between host subcounties (see src-ubos-nphc-2024-geo), the crosswalk's parish rows count 10,465 exact, 98 fuzzy, 144 unmatched (the 123 settlement-unit parishes and Lubya are no longer rows).

title: UBOS National Population and Housing Census 2024 — sub-region profile reports (list of report titles)
note: Identifies UBOS's current 16 named sub-regions (Acholi, Ankole, Buganda, Bugisu, Bukedi, Bunyoro, Busoga, Karamoja, Kigezi, Lango, Madi, Rwenzori, Sebei, Teso, Tooro, West Nile) plus a separate Kampala Capital City profile — used as the taxonomy for data/subregions.csv and the new subregion_id field on districts/cities. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: every direct WebFetch attempt against ubos.org and statistics.ubos.org failed with a TLS 'unable to verify the first certificate' error from the fetch tool used; the report-title list and the Madi/Rwenzori/Sebei 2024 splits (see src-subregion-district-mapping-2026) were corroborated via web-search-engine snippets quoting/describing those UBOS pages/PDFs, not a direct primary-document fetch. Treat the UBOS attribution here as search-engine-mediated, not independently verified the way src-ec-admin-units-2022 was — a primary-source re-fetch (e.g. from a browser) would strengthen this. FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-21): that primary-source re-fetch happened, for a separate population-data task — a plain `curl` request with a browser User-Agent and `-k` reached ubos.org and statistics.ubos.org fine (see src-ubos-nphc2024-final-report), confirming the original TLS failure was specific to the WebFetch tool's certificate handling, not a real block. The Final Report PDF fetched then independently confirms this subregion taxonomy: its own Table 2.1 (Population Distribution by sub Region) lists exactly these same 17 groups (16 named sub-regions + Kampala Capital City) with 2024 population figures for each — a genuine primary-document confirmation this entry didn't have when first written.

title: District-to-subregion composition (Wikipedia sub-region articles + citypopulation.de aggregation)
note: Used to assign all 136 districts (plus Kampala and the 10 second-generation cities) to one of the 17 UBOS-named subregions in data/subregions.csv / data/districts.csv / data/cities.csv. Every district, including every post-2015 split (e.g. Karenga from Kaabong, Kwania from Apac, Madi-Okollo/Terego from Arua, Obongi from Moyo, Kazo from Kiruhura, Kikuube from Hoima, Rubanda/Rukiga from Kabale, Rwampara from Mbarara, Kassanda/Kyankwanzi/Kyotera from Mubende/Kiboga/Rakai), was found named explicitly in at least one of these sources alongside its parent district in the same subregion group — no district's placement was inferred purely from its parent without direct confirmation. Cross-checked two ways per subregion (a Wikipedia sub-region article's district list against citypopulation.de's independent administrative breakdown); all matched with no contradictions. Confidence: verified, on the same basis the project already uses for region_id (2+ independent, currently-maintained secondary sources in agreement), not on a fetched UBOS primary document — see src-ubos-subregions-2024's caveat. This is inherently a coarser, more contestable classification than administrative boundaries (sub-region membership reflects a historical/cultural majority, not a claim that a district's population is ethnically homogeneous).

title: geoBoundaries — Uganda ADM3 (labeled 'District')
note: UPDATE 2026-10-17 (final): NOT a source of any published boundary. Used for exactly one thing — the COASTLINE of the land mask in scripts/ingest-ubos-boundaries.mjs. UBOS's polygons follow legal boundaries out into the lakes, so water = UBOS's country outline minus the union of these features (its separate 'Lake Victoria' polygon removed, small gaps filled), INTERSECTED with Natural Earth's lake extents (src-natural-earth-10m-lakes). The intersection is essential: this layer's western border is wrong, and without it Bundibugyo's Semliki strip and parts of Kasese came out as 'water' and 41 parishes vanished. Why it is no longer the district geometry: a direct comparison found these polygons materially wrong for many districts (only 12 of 135 had intersection-over-union >= 0.9 with their UBOS/COD-AB counterpart; Kampala came out at 351 km2 vs ~189 official, having swallowed Kira and Kasangati, which are in Wakiso; Pader town fell inside Agago; Wakiso came out at 1,747 km2). The 136/136 match described below was a NAME match only and never checked the shapes. Terego is no longer taken from here either — UBOS's 2024 district layer includes it. The original note follows. ORIGINAL NOTE (2026-07-21): USED for data/geo/districts.geojson. Downloaded directly (550KB raw GeoJSON, not a summarizer pass) and diffed all 137 shapeName values against data/districts.csv programmatically: 136/136 districts matched (5 minor spelling variants — Madi Okollo/Ssembabule matched via existing slug/alias handling; Kalanga->Kalangala, Kitagwenga->Kitagwenda, Rubirzi->Rubirizi needed an explicit override, see the since-deleted scripts/ingest-district-boundaries.mjs), plus one extraneous non-district 'Lake Victoria' water-body polygon (dropped). Critically, this 2020-vintage file already includes Terego District — the split that Statoids/Wikipedia/the MoLG list all missed (see the 136-district entry above) — making it a better vintage than HDX's district layer for this specific purpose. Licensed CC0 1.0 (public domain, no attribution required) per geoBoundaries' own per-level metadata API. Sanity-checked post-ingestion: bounding box (29.58-34.99°E, -1.47-4.22°N) and total area (~211,760 km²) match Uganda's known geography, and area is exactly conserved between the district layer and the region layer dissolved from it (see src-region-boundary-dissolve below).

title: Natural Earth 1:10m Physical Vectors — Lakes (ne_10m_lakes), v5.1.2
note: USED for lake extents only. Public domain. The 7 features covering Uganda (Lakes Albert, Victoria, Edward, Kyoga, Kwania, Bunyonyi and one unnamed) are committed at data/legacy/provenance/geo/ne-10m-lakes-uganda.geojson. In scripts/ingest-ubos-boundaries.mjs they are buffered 3 km (to reach geoBoundaries' finer shoreline) and intersected with 'UBOS country outline minus geoBoundaries land' (src-geoboundaries-uga-adm3), so only area that is actually lake is cut out of the UBOS polygons, which follow legal boundaries into the water. Without this intersection, geoBoundaries' wrong western border turned Bundibugyo's Semliki strip and parts of Kasese into 'water' and 41 parishes vanished.

title: geoBoundaries — Uganda ADM1 ('Region')
note: Evaluated, deliberately NOT used. Confirmed via direct fetch to be exactly the 4 regions (e.g. 'Northern Region'), 2017 vintage. Not ingested because it's licensed ODbL 1.0 (share-alike) — a second, stricter license — and because dissolving our own district polygons by region_id (see src-region-boundary-dissolve) guarantees the region shapes can never drift out of sync with this project's own region_id assignments in data/districts.csv. Kept as a source-of-record only in case a future cross-check against an independently-drawn region boundary is useful.

title: Region boundaries dissolved from data/geo/districts.geojson
publisher: This project (derived, not an external source)
note: data/geo/regions.geojson is not sourced from anywhere external — it's produced by scripts/build-region-boundaries.mjs, which groups the district features by region_id and unions each group's geometry with @turf/turf (a devDependency used only at data-prep time, never shipped in the published package). UPDATE 2026-10-17 (final): the district features are now built bottom-up from UBOS's own 2024/2025 polygons (src-ubos-nphc-2024-geo, src-ubos-bec-2025-geo; see scripts/ingest-ubos-boundaries.mjs), so the regions are processed UBOS data too (cite UBOS — see LICENSE-DATA.md). Earlier versions of this note described the CC0 geoBoundaries district layer (src-geoboundaries-uga-adm3) and then, briefly, an OCHA COD-AB one; both are superseded. The union runs over districts that were simplified as part of one shared TopoJSON topology (scripts/lib/topo.mjs) — the original per-feature turf.simplify left hairline gaps between neighbouring districts, which surfaced as ~1,513 slit holes in the dissolved regions. Measured on the current build: regions total 215,511 km2 against 215,579 km2 for the districts they're dissolved from (within 0.03%); Central, Eastern and Western are MultiPolygons (non-contiguous island districts, e.g. Kalangala/Buvuma), Northern a single Polygon. Every output feature is rewound for d3-geo's spherical convention — turf.union returns planar-wound rings, which d3-geo reads as 'the globe minus this polygon' — and scripts/validate.mjs fails any boundary feature whose exterior ring is counter-clockwise. SUB-REGIONS (added 2026-10-17): the same script also unions the districts by subregion_id into data/geo/subregions.geojson (17 features, 215,530 km2), so the sub-region shapes can't drift from subregion_id in data/districts.csv either; scripts/validate.mjs expects 17.

title: geoBoundaries — Uganda ADM2 ('County')
note: UPDATE 2026-10-17: county polygons ARE now included — all 322 of 322, each the union of its subcounties' land in the UBOS-based bottom-up build (see src-ubos-nphc-2024-geo; an intermediate same-day build had 118 from COD-AB ADM3). So the last sentence of the original note below no longer holds. This geoBoundaries layer itself stays rejected. ORIGINAL NOTE: Evaluated and rejected for county-level boundaries. Per geoBoundaries' own metadata: 151 counties, 2006 vintage — stale and short of this project's own EC-derived 322 counties/constituencies (see src-ec-admin-units-2022) by more than half. No other free source of standalone county polygon geometry was found either; this project's county *data* (names) comes from EC gazetteer text, not from any geometry source. County-level boundaries are not included in this dataset.

title: geoBoundaries — Uganda ADM4 ('Sub-county')
note: UPDATE 2026-10-17 (final): NO LONGER USED. Earlier the same day it had been demoted to a name-only fallback behind COD-AB ADM4 (to which it added 0 polygons — all 1,253 of its unique-name matches were already covered, since it is the same UBOS 2019 subcounty data: 1,521 features here vs 1,520 in COD-AB's admin4, the same tier, not a coincidence). The subcounty layer is now built from UBOS's own 2024 polygons (src-ubos-nphc-2024-geo) and scripts/ingest-subcounty-boundaries.mjs, which read this file, has been deleted. The raw file may still sit (gitignored) in data/legacy/provenance/geo/, read by nothing. The original note follows; its 1,249 / 57.0% figures describe the 0.9.0 build. ORIGINAL NOTE (2026-07-21): USED for data/geo/subcountys.geojson (previously evaluated and deferred in an earlier pass; brought in on explicit instruction to surface all available data now rather than wait for a complete source). 1,521 features, 2019 vintage, CC BY 3.0 IGO, ~47.7MB raw (downloaded directly via curl, not WebFetch, which had hit a size cap on this file previously). Carries no parent-district attribute, so matching against data/ec/administrative_units_ec2022.json's subcounty/town_council/division records had to be done by bare name: 1,249 of 1,521 features matched a UNIQUE current unit (confirmed correct via spot-check, e.g. 'Bar Dege Division'/'Laroo Division'/'Pece Division' resolving to real Gulu City divisions), 165 had no name match at all, and 102 (42 distinct names) were excluded as ambiguous — the same subcounty/division name is reused across 2+ districts for ~5% of this project's own units, and this source gives no way to disambiguate. Net: 1,249/2,191 = 57.0% coverage of this project's verified subcounty-tier units. Simplified (turf, tolerance 0.001°) from 36.4MB matched down to ~3.2MB for package size.

title: RETRACTED — Uganda - Subnational Administrative Boundaries — admin4 layer (previously misidentified as parish-level; it is subcounty-tier)
publisher: OCHA / Humanitarian Data Exchange (data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-uga), sourced from UBOS
url: https://data.humdata.org/api/3/action/package_show?id=cod-ab-uga (CKAN API, returns the geojson.zip resource URL directly)
note: RETRACTED 2026-10-17 — NO LONGER USED; scripts/ingest-parish-boundaries.mjs has been deleted. (data/geo/parishs.geojson was briefly an empty FeatureCollection; later the same day it was refilled with REAL parish polygons — 10,634 of 10,717 — from UBOS's Baseline Education Census 2025, see src-ubos-bec-2025-geo. Nothing from this retracted layer is in it.) The claim below that this layer is 'genuinely parish-level' was WRONG: COD-AB's admin4 is SUBCOUNTY-tier. Evidence: it contains Kampala's five divisions (Central/Kawempe/Makindye/Nakawa/Rubaga Division, codes UG10080101-05), which are subcounty-tier units; its P-codes are 8-digit subcounty-shaped codes nested under 6-digit county codes; and COD-AB Uganda has only ADM0-ADM4 (country, 4 regions, 135 districts, 203 counties, 1,520 subcounties) — no parish or village level at all. The attributes never said 'parish': reading adm3_name as subcounty and adm4_name as parish was off by one tier (adm3_name is the county — e.g. the first raw record is adm3_name 'Moroto', Alebtong's Moroto County, adm4_name 'Abako', a subcounty). The ~1,520-feature 'coincidence' with geoBoundaries' 1,521-feature subcounty layer was the tell: same tier. The 423 'matches' were therefore subcounty polygons attached to parishes that happen to share their subcounty's name (e.g. parish:alebtong-abia-abia received the outline of the whole of Abia subcounty). This same COD-AB admin4 layer was then briefly used, correctly, as SUBCOUNTY geometry, and is now used only for its P-codes — see src-hdx-cod-ab-uga. Entry id kept so existing references don't dangle. The original (incorrect) note follows for the record. ORIGINAL NOTE (2026-07-21): USED for data/geo/parishs.geojson. This is the SAME dataset already documented at src-hdx-cod-ab-uga (previously rejected for NAME data at admin3/admin4 for being stale/incomplete), but re-evaluated here specifically for its GEOMETRY, per explicit instruction to bring in all available data even where partial. 1,520 features, valid_on 2020-08-24, CC BY-IGO. Confirmed via its own attributes (adm1_name=region, adm2_name=district, adm3_name=subcounty, adm4_name=parish — e.g. a sample record has adm2_name:'Zombo', a real current district) that this tier is genuinely parish-level, NOT the same tier as geoBoundaries' similarly-numbered-but-differently-scoped ADM4 'Sub-county' layer (src-geoboundaries-uga-adm4) despite both having ~1,520 features — a coincidence that would be easy to mistake for the same data if not checked directly. Matched on (district_name, parish_name) pairs against this project's own EC-derived parish/ward records: 423 of 1,520 matched a unique current parish/ward (3.95% of this project's 10,717 verified parishes/wards — a genuinely thin result, not an ingestion bug), 8 didn't resolve to any current district name, 1,083 resolved to a real district but no matching parish name (the 2020 vintage predates significant parish-level reorganization), 6 excluded as ambiguous. See data/legacy/provenance/geo/README.md and scripts/ingest-parish-boundaries.mjs. Simplified the same way as the subcounty layer.

title: Roads of Uganda (HOTOSM export)
publisher: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team, via HDX Raw Data API (data.humdata.org/dataset/hotosm_uga_roads), sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (Geofabrik snapshot)
note: USED for data/geo/roads.geojson. ODC-ODbL license, snapshot dated 2026-06-22. Raw export: 681,317 features (lines/points/polygons combined) — 98.8% have no `name` tag at all (only 4,072 distinct names nationally), and the two largest highway=* categories are 'path' (237,482) and 'track' (95,304): informal footpaths/tracks, not roads. This project ships only the 'major road network' cut — highway in {motorway, motorway_link, trunk, trunk_link, primary, primary_link, secondary, secondary_link, tertiary, tertiary_link} — 10,721 features, ~29% named, ~3.6MB simplified. A wider 'classified roads' cut (adds unclassified+residential) was evaluated and rejected as a default: 278,185 features, 77.8MB, still ~89% unnamed. Neither the full 681K-feature raw export nor the 278K classified-roads cut is shipped, but both remain directly reproducible from the cited URL — see data/legacy/provenance/roads/README.md and scripts/ingest-roads.mjs. Parsed with the pure-JS `shapefile` npm package (dev-only dependency) since no GDAL/ogr2ogr was available in this environment; the .dbf attribute table alone is ~1.3GB, streamed rather than loaded whole. Deliberately NOT joined to any administrative unit — OSM carries no district/subcounty tagging, and this dataset does not attempt to compute one via spatial join in this pass.

title: GADM — Database of Global Administrative Areas, Uganda
note: Evaluated and rejected outright, regardless of geometry quality. GADM's own license page states redistribution or commercial use is not allowed without prior permission — directly incompatible with this project's CC BY 4.0 / CC0 posture. Also suspected (not fully confirmed — GADM's per-level pages are JS-rendered and count wasn't independently opened) to simply repackage the same stale COD-AB source as HDX: its reported ADM3/ADM4 counts (208/1,520) exactly match HDX's.

title: OpenStreetMap WikiProject Uganda — District Boundaries status page
note: A genuine, actively-maintained alternative for district-level boundaries (all 146 district-equivalents self-reported 'Complete' at admin_level=4 as of the page's 2026-03-05 revision), ODbL-licensed. Not used: originally because geoBoundaries' CC0 layer already covered all 136 districts with a simpler license; since 2026-10-17 every boundary level comes from UBOS's own 2024/2025 polygons (src-ubos-nphc-2024-geo, src-ubos-bec-2025-geo) instead, and OSM's ODbL share-alike terms would still be the stricter choice. Not independently spot-checked polygon-by-polygon — this is a self-reported project-status table, not something this pass validated at the geometry level. The same page states subcounty/county boundaries are 'future work' and lower levels are mapped mostly as point nodes, not polygons — confirms those tiers aren't available from OSM either, for now.

title: Ministry of Water and Environment — WEIS GeoServer
publisher: Ministry of Water and Environment, Uganda (weis.mwe.go.ug)
note: Deliberately NOT used, though reachable: MWE's terms forbid automated access without written permission (and forbid commercial reuse). Identified by the research/observatory session as a high-value source — catchments, water points, wetlands, and 44,034 village polygons, the only village-level geometry seen anywhere — but not fetched, and nothing from it is in this dataset. Written permission would be needed first (the observatory session's docs/observatory/USER-ACTIONS.md drafts the request).

title: Parish Boundaries: Uganda, 2010
publisher: Uganda Bureau of Statistics, hosted by Stanford Earth Sciences Library / AGSL
note: Evaluated and rejected for parish-level boundaries. A real, public-domain UBOS parish polygon shapefile exists here, but it's 2010/2012 vintage — well over a decade before this project's own verified 10,717-parish EC gazetteer figure, from before roughly half of today's districts existed. The catalog page doesn't publish a feature count, so an exact coverage percentage couldn't be computed, but given the district count alone has more than doubled since 2010, well under half of today's parishes are likely represented. Not ingested. UPDATE 2026-10-17: superseded outright — UBOS's own current parish polygons (Baseline Education Census 2025, src-ubos-bec-2025-geo) now supply 10,634 of the 10,717 EC parishes.

title: "uganda_village_shapefile" (unlicensed GitHub repository)
publisher: GitHub user justinelliotmeyers, surfaced via a June 2026 'Revolutionary GIS' blog post
note: Evaluated and rejected, the only candidate found for village-level geometry at all. Not trusted from the filename alone — the raw .shp/.dbf headers were inspected byte-by-byte directly: shape type 5 (genuine Polygon geometry, not points), 44,034 records, with a real VILLAGE/PARISH/SUBCOUNTY/COUNTY/DISTRICT field structure consistent with authentic UBOS cartographic data. But: 44,034 is only ~62% of this project's own verified 71,230-village count (src-ec-admin-units-2022, July 2022), the repository has no README, license, or description anywhere (an anonymous single-commit upload), and the '2011' vintage implied by the filename could not be independently confirmed — the .dbf's internal last-modified field just reflects a 2026-06-29 re-save, not original survey date. Given no license and material staleness/incompleteness, this is documented as evaluated-and-rejected, the same way this project already treats other real-but-unusable candidates, rather than ingested. No village/cell-level boundary data is included in this dataset. UPDATE 2026-10-17: the research/observatory session's catalogue lists exactly 44,034 village polygons on the Ministry of Water and Environment's WEIS GeoServer (src-mwe-weis-geoserver-not-used) — the same record count as this upload, which suggests (not confirmed) that this is a copy of that layer. If so, it still can't be used: MWE's terms forbid automated access without written permission and forbid commercial reuse.

title: National Population and Housing Census 2024 — Final Report, Volume 1 (Main)
note: USED for data/population/uganda-nphc-2024-population.csv (146 rows: 136 districts + 10 cities, actual final 2024 census counts, not a projection). Every earlier WebFetch-tool request to ubos.org in this project failed with a TLS certificate error; a plain `curl` request with a browser User-Agent and -k succeeded, revealing this was a tool-side TLS chain issue, not a real access block (see data/legacy/provenance/population/README.md for the full fetch story). Extracted Tables 2.4 A-D (Total Population by District and City, Central/Eastern/Northern/Western) using `pdftotext -table` mode (plain `-layout` mode badly misaligned this table's columns; -table extracted every row correctly). Validated three independent ways with zero discrepancies: (1) male+female=total for all 146 rows: exact for every row; (2) cross-checked against the report's own prose ('Wakiso... 3,411,177... Kalangala... 74,411 people'): exact match; (3) summed all 146 rows' male/female/total columns independently and reproduced the report's separately-stated national total (22,314,289 / 23,591,128 / 45,905,417) to the person across all three columns. All 146 names resolved to this project's own district/city ids with zero unresolved and zero missing (the report already uses this project's existing 'Luweero'/'Ssembabule' aliases). Superior to src-hdx-cod-ps-uga-not-used (2023 projection) precisely because it's the actual current census count, per the project's currency-first sourcing standard. No explicit copyright/license statement was found anywhere in the report; treated as public government statistical data consistent with how other UBOS content is handled in this project, but flagged rather than assumed — see LICENSE-DATA.md.

title: Uganda - Subnational Population Statistics
publisher: OCHA / Humanitarian Data Exchange (data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ps-uga), sourced from UBOS
note: Candidate for a district population layer, considered and then superseded — not ingested. 2023-projected population, age/sex disaggregated, national/region/district levels, CSV+XLSX, CC BY-IGO, last updated 2023-11-09, explicitly built on the old 135-district system (would have needed the same Terego reconciliation solved once already for districts.csv). Superseded by src-ubos-nphc2024-final-report once it turned out ubos.org was directly reachable after all (see that entry) — the actual 2024 census count is more current and more authoritative than a 2023 projection, so this dataset was never ingested.

title: WorldPop — Population Counts for Uganda
note: Candidate for a future population layer, not ingested. 100m-resolution gridded, UN-adjusted population raster (GeoTIFF), not tied to any fixed admin schema — would need zonal-statistics GIS processing (e.g. summing raster cells within each district/subcounty polygon) rather than being a drop-in CSV join. More flexible than src-hdx-cod-ps-uga (works with any future boundary layer, not just district) but meaningfully more engineering effort. UPDATE 2026-10-17: subcounty and county population no longer need it — UBOS's own NPHC 2024 per-subcounty counts are now used (see src-ubos-nphc-2024-geo, data/population/ubos-nphc-2024-subcounty.csv). Still the candidate for anything finer (parish, village), not ingested.

title: location.csv (user-supplied legacy dataset)
publisher: Unknown/original provenance not documented by user
note: The project's original seed file (135-row header implies district+county+subcounty, but only covered 110 of 135 districts and the county column duplicates the subcounty name for most rows, i.e. it does not contain real county data). Migrated as-is to data/legacy/subcounties_legacy_source.csv for reconciliation, not treated as verified.
